description: Thai domestic upstream packaging survey: five tracks, verification checks, completeness critic. Copied from the workflow journal in journal order. Singapore and Korea excluded.

results.summary: Thailand-domestic survey of upstream packaging for Product A (leaf-wrapped frozen coconut-pandan drink with PET pouch) and Product B (250 ml unsweetened UHT soy drink), searched live on 18 Oct 2026 after reading the four rework files. No Thai supplier price was found for any packaging option except one retail bagasse box (HomePro, THB 2.50 per piece, out of stock at capture). Every other row is cost_basis none or proxy (EU, UK, Sweden, US), labelled as such. Product A candidates: bagasse or molded-pulp containers (BPE/Gracz, deSter, Thai Paper Co Fest Bio and Fest Chill), PE- or PBS-coated paper cups (TPBI/TMP, Thai Anbao), and PLA-coated paper (no Thai maker confirmed). None of these is a barrier by itself. rework/31 predicts PE strips pandan aroma, so PE-faced cups conflict with Product A; PBS and PLA were not assessed. Product B: SIG aseptic cartons have Thai precedent (Tofusan 2020, Benefitt), but no carton price was found. PET 250 ml options (Petform, Envicco rPET) have no Thai price; only non-Thai PET proxies were found. Regulation: TIS 2948-2562 (food-contact paper) requires a TIS licence and mark. Its enforcement date conflicts: 22 June 2026 in a Tilleke article (29 Apr 2026); 22 June 2027 in an SGS note (Jul 2026) and a Chemlinked entry for amendment No. 2 B.E. 2569. This must be checked in the Royal Gazette. The compostable product standards TIS 17088-2562 and TIS 2884 Part 1-2560 (PLA containers) come from one secondary source (PTT GC, Jul 2025, citing TISI), and TIS 17088 has an unresolved 2555 vs 2562 edition conflict. No Thai bio-based content standard was found; the only bio-based methods cited are ASTM D6866 and EN 16785-1. Inference, not sourced: a whole-pack compostable claim is unlikely to hold while a PET pouch is in the pack, since PET is not compostable.

No frozen or cold-chain test data for any paper, bagasse or molded-pulp container was found.
Dated Thai news on the TIS paper standard (dailynews, Apr 2025) gives an old December 2025 timeline; treated as stale and not used.

Excluded as not packaging cost: a Lazada soy-milk pack price (product retail price) and a HomePro 1.2 L PET water bottle at THB 69 (not 250 ml). rework/04 is a beverage price audit with no packaging cost data, so it was not used for packaging.

results.summary: Thai domestic-only survey of packaging cost levers for Product A (leaf-wrapped frozen drink with PET pouch) and Product B (250 ml UHT soy). One candidate: drop plastic straws and thin plastic cups, which the 2565 step of the official PCD roadmap restricts. Most others are holds: the draft EPR Act (no plastic or carton fee published; the only draft rate is 0.67 THB/kg for glass, used as a proxy), the national-park sales-channel question for the PET pouch, the SME co-payment (requires SME registration), TISTR services (no published fees), and DIPROM (2026 prize round closed). BOI is rejected for scale and the EEC SME estate for not being a packaging pool. No price was invented; cost_basis is "none" except the glass EPR proxy. Primary Thai pages were read for the PCD roadmap, the DNP notice summary, BOI PR156/2569 and the BDS homepage; other items rest on secondary news.

Thailand-domestic scope only; Singapore and Korea items dropped (Humi Pak, a Singapore gel maker, was not used). All prices are online retail listings read on 18 Oct 2026, not supplier quotes, and most listing pages are undated. Cheapest per unit at small volume with a Thai price: 0 C-class gel packs at THB 18-25 each (igloogel THB 18, size not stated; 250 g at THB 25) and foam boxes at THB 25-40 (Lazada listings, EPS and size not confirmed). A foam box plus two 250 g gel packs (about 0.5 kg, close to the 0.6 kg in rework/22) comes to about THB 75-90 per shipment at listing prices (derived). The only frozen-hold case in the repo thaw screen is an EPS-walled insulated cooler with gel packs: half-thawed at about 3.2 h, against about 1.5 h bare in 30 C still air (rework/06). No new thaw run was done. The thaw answers for other options are direction only, from sourced conductivities and derived UA ratios. Sub-zero PCM and dry ice would hold the product frozen longer, but no Thai sub-zero PCM price was found, and dry ice costs about THB 130 per box on dry ice alone and is a handling hazard. Molded pulp: no Thai insulated supplier, and pulp conducts more heat than EPS. Reusable hard boxes list at THB 612-759 and reusable soft bags at THB 21.96-1,150, with break-even around 15-45 uses against a THB 25-40 single-use box (derived). No Thai deposit-return precedent for insulated boxes was found; the only Thai precedent is Yakult's distributor-sold cooler bag (2022).

results.reason: The cost indication "No cost" is not on either cited page, and the entry gives no basis for it. The ONEP summary states a fine of up to 100,000 baht for breaches, which I confirmed, but a fine is a penalty to violators, not a packaging price or compliance cost. Neither source gives any packaging cost, price, or cost-neutrality statement. The second cited source, the PCD PDF, is a national plastic-waste roadmap infographic (B.E. 2561-2573). It does not mention national parks, a penalty, a cost, or the 5 April 2022 notice, so it does not support the entry's national-park ban. The food-contact entry "n/a" is not a positive claim, so the food-contact criterion is not triggered, although the notice does cover plastic food boxes and foam food containers. The out-of-date criterion is not triggered: searches found no amendment or repeal, though I could not check the Royal Gazette text directly. The supplier criterion does not apply, since this is a regulation and not a supplied material.
results.evidence: 1) ONEP page, "7 April 2565 ... ห้ามนำโฟม-พลาสติก ใช้ครั้งเดียว เข้าอุทยานฯ ฝ่าฝืนปรับหนึ่งแสน" (https://www.onep.go.th/7-%E0%B9%80%E0%B8%A1%E0%B8%A9%E0%B8%B2%E0%B8%A2%E0%B8%99-2565-%E0%B8%AA%E0%B8%B2%E0%B8%A2%E0%B9%81%E0%B8%84%E0%B8%A1%E0%B8%9B%E0%B9%8C%E0%B8%95%E0%B9%89%E0%B8%AD%E0%B8%87%E0%B8%A3%E0%B8%B9%E0%B9%89/): fetched and read. It gives the gazette date as 5 April (year from the 2565 title), the issuing body as the Department of National Parks, Wildlife and Plant Conservation, and the banned items as plastic carry bags under 36 microns, plastic food boxes, thin single-use cups, straws, and spoons and forks. The penalty is a fine not exceeding 100,000 baht under section 20 read with section 47 of the National Park Act B.E. 2562. It states no price, cost, or cost-impact figure and no food-contact or food-grade statement. 2) PCD PDF (https://www.pcd.go.th/wp-content/uploads/2021/10/pcdnew-2021-10-19_08-59-31_527174.pdf): fetched and read as a rendered page. It is a one-page infographic, "Roadmap การจัดการขยะพลาสติก พ.ศ. 2561-2573" (Thailand's Roadmap on Plastic Waste Management 2018-2030). Its 2565 band lists foam food containers, plastic straws, bags under 36 microns, and thin plastic cups. It has no national-park reference, no penalty, no cost, no food-contact text, and no gazette date. 3) Search for amendments or repeal in 2025-2026 (Thai queries): no amendment or repeal found, and current status not confirmed. 4) Royal Gazette text: not retrieved. A search summary of the DNP news item (http://news.dnp.go.th/news/15420) reports a notice dated 11 February 2565, gazetted 5 April 2565, effective the day after publication, with a penalty of up to 100,000 baht under sections 20 and 47 of the 2562 Act. I could not open that DNP page directly because of a self-signed certificate error. 5) Date and penalty claims in the entry are consistent with the ONEP and DNP-summary evidence. The "No cost" claim and the food-contact "n/a" are not supported or contradicted by any primary text checked.

Banana leaf is the strongest candidate: the best dated public price is 40 to 70 THB/kg at the Oct to Nov 2024 festival peak, with a 9 to 10 THB/kg farm-gate from the Khlong Krachong group (Sukhothai) in the same article. Rice paper, nori and edible film fail the leaf-wrap claim and have no reliable Thai price (proxies only). No Thai leaf-prep cost was found. Pesticide residue status: Notification No. 460 (B.E. 2568), in force 22 July 2025; no leaf-specific food-contact rule was found. Cost levers: buy off-peak within the May to December harvest; contract with the Khlong Krachong group under the 2017 Act; mechanised forming exists but not for cutting; dried leaf sells at about 200 THB/kg, so it is not a cheap leaf bank. The next step is a dated Talad Thai wholesale price, which the official board does not carry.

Thailand-domestic survey of inner pouch film options for product A (leaf-wrapped frozen coconut-pandan drink). No supported cost data exists, so every number is either a labelled proxy or 'none'. Antimony-free PET stays the only candidate: it has Thai film sources (Toyobo Thailand heat-seal grade, Polyplex and SRF in Rayong), a Thai listing under Notification 435, and vendor freezer claims. Thai film sources exist for PE, PP and PET, a partial lead exists for EVOH (TPN FlexPak, unconfirmed), and no Thai source was found for an aluminium-free paper pouch. No Thai converter publishes a minimum order quantity, and no Thai THB/kg film price was found. Proxy resin prices, converted at 33.57 THB/USD (moneyexchangerate.org, 11 Oct 2026): PET film about 58 to 66 THB/kg (global BOPET projection), LDPE film about 46 to 50 THB/kg (Southeast Asia CFR, 2 Sep 2026), PLA resin about 82 THB/kg (Southeast Asia, 8 Jun 2026). Regulation: the 16 Sep 2026 draft amendment to Notification 435 would add EVOH and PLA (among PBS, PBSA, PPO), so both need the unlisted-plastic route today; PBAT is not named. Paper enters Thai scope through a Feb 2026 draft revising Announcement 92, and a coated paper also falls under the plastic rule. Freezer: PP rejected; PE and PET supported by vendor and older test evidence; PLA likely brittle; EVOH, PBAT and paper untested. Taste (virtual model): PE and PP predicted to strip aroma; PET (0.18 percent uptake) and EVOH (0.03 percent) favoured; PLA, PBAT and paper not modelled. Product B (soy UHT) is outside this track and was not assessed.

options.fit_notes: Freezer: vendor claims only. Standard PET 'can typically handle temperatures down to minus 10 degrees Fahrenheit'; freezer-grade impact-modified PET stays ductile 'even down to minus 30 degrees Celsius'; plain PET can crystallize in the freezer, so amorphous APET is the usual freezer grade (Inline Plastics, 20 Aug 2025: https://www.inlineplastics.com/blog/food-packaging-in-freezers/). Taste: virtual model gives 0.18 percent aroma uptake in 2 h, against over 100 percent for PE and PP (rework/31); EVOH is lower at 0.03 percent. Antimony-free catalyst is the working spec (rework/32); titanium catalysts are sold as antimony replacements (Clariant, vendor claim). Fat content and migration test remain open.
